rubrics.rubric: Does Complaint_Triage_Response_Package.docx provide a complete, policy-grounded customer response for every open complaint ticket?
criterion: Every open Ticket ID in customer_complaint_emails.xlsx has a distinct customer-facing response.
Each response cites every applicable store_policies.docx section by its exact title.
Each response states the policy terms that control the proposed resolution.
Each response addresses the customer's requested remedy or explains the next verification step.
Each response uses a professional and empathetic tone.
Each response provides concrete next steps.

rubrics.rubric: Does every internal Triage Note accurately connect the complaint, catalog, sales evidence, and recommended catalog action?
criterion: Every open ticket has a distinct internal Triage Note.
Each note checks the complained product against current_product_listings.csv.
Each note states the catalog-match basis.
Each note reports product-level margin context from store_sales_data.csv when a reliable match exists.
Each note explicitly records no reliable match or insufficient margin data when the sales source cannot support a product match.
Each note recommends correcting the listing, removing the product, or escalating the issue.
Each recommendation is justified by the complaint, catalog, and available margin evidence.

rubrics.rubric: Does Integrated_Performance_Dashboard.xlsx contain the exact three required sheets with correct profitability and traffic-funnel calculations?
criterion: The workbook contains exactly Profit Margin Analysis, Traffic-to-Sales Funnel, and Underperformer Crosswalk.
Profit Margin Analysis has one row per Sub-Category.
Profit Margin Analysis contains every required column.
Profit Margin % is calculated as aggregated Profit divided by aggregated Sales for each Sub-Category.
Average Discount is calculated from store_sales_data.csv.
Order Count is calculated from store_sales_data.csv.
Traffic-to-Sales Funnel has one row per Month and VisitorType combination.
Traffic-to-Sales Funnel contains every required column.
Revenue Conversion Rate is calculated as the percentage of sessions whose Revenue value is true.
Sessions reconcile to the complete website_traffic_data.csv.
All displayed traffic averages reconcile to the complete website_traffic_data.csv.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Underperformer Crosswalk correctly identify the ten lowest-margin products and check each against the current catalog?
criterion: Sales and Profit are aggregated consistently at Product Name level before profit margin is calculated.
The sheet contains exactly ten product rows selected by ascending Profit Margin %.
Each row includes Product Name, Category, Sub-Category, Sales, Profit, Profit Margin %, and Listing Match Status.
Listing Match Status is based on an explicit comparison with current_product_listings.csv.
Unmatched or ambiguous names are reported as such rather than forced into an unsupported match.

rubrics.rubric: Does the sentiment audit compute the required department and class statistics and derive complaint themes from the complete reviews dataset?
criterion: Average Rating is calculated by Department Name over all usable customer_reviews.csv rows.
Recommendation rate is calculated by Department Name over all usable customer_reviews.csv rows.
Average Rating is calculated by Class Name over all usable customer_reviews.csv rows.
Recommendation rate is calculated by Class Name over all usable customer_reviews.csv rows.
Review count is calculated by Class Name over all usable customer_reviews.csv rows.
The lowest-rated class ranking excludes classes with fewer than 30 reviews.
The eligible classes are sorted by average rating ascending, recommendation rate ascending, review count descending, and Class Name ascending.
The three lowest eligible classes are identified from the displayed calculation.
Recurring complaint themes for those classes are supported by quotations from actual review text.
Small-sample classes are treated as caveats rather than mixed into the ranked three.

rubrics.rubric: Does Customer_Sentiment_Catalog_Alignment_Audit.pdf meet the required format and connect review evidence to catalog language and prioritized recommendations?
criterion: The PDF is approximately two to three pages.
The four required sections appear in the specified order.
For product types present in both sources, the audit quotes specific listing language and specific review language.
Each cross-check states whether the listing addresses or ignores the cited pain point.
The audit provides three to five prioritized recommendations.
Each recommendation links a specific catalog-copy change to a documented customer pain point.

rubrics.rubric: Does optimized_product_listings.csv preserve the source catalog while making every required, evidence-grounded listing and feed-field update?
criterion: The file has the exact required filename.
Every row from current_product_listings.csv is preserved.
Every original column from current_product_listings.csv is preserved.
Listing Change Justification is present for every source row.
Listing Change Justification is non-empty for every source row.
Body (HTML) copy describes product benefits that are supported by the source catalog, complaint, review, or sales evidence without unsupported superlatives or claims.
Body (HTML) copy uses product-specific names, types, materials, uses, or audience terms supported by the source data; keyword repetition or keyword stuffing is not required.
Body (HTML) copy is consistent with the available complaint and review evidence.
Claims contradicted by evidence are removed or qualified.
Sizing or fit guidance is added where the review evidence supports it.
Every previously empty SEO Title field is completed.
Every previously empty SEO Description field is completed.
Every previously empty Google Shopping field is completed with a value appropriate to the product or an explicit applicable placeholder accepted by the feed format.
Each justification cites a ticket ID, review theme, sales finding, or a documented source-data limitation.
